messages.text: How Grant is using his experience in Charlton homecoming

metadata.summary: "It's nice to be home," is Karlan Grant's reply when asked how the last few months have been sign he re-joined Charlton in the summer.
metadata.content: Karlan Grant: Charlton forward on returning to the club and facing Norwich on Red, White and Black weekend | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Karlan Grant: Charlton forward on returning to the club and facing Norwich on Red, White and Black weekend Karlan Grant has returned to Charlton after seven years away; this weekend celebrates the club's Red, White and Black campaign and the EFL's Together for Racism fixture; watch Charlton vs Norwich live on Sky Sports Football and Main Event from 11.30am; kick-off 12.30pm Charlotte Marsh Senior Football Journalist Thursday 22 October 2026 17:44, UK "It's nice to be home," is Karlan Grant's reply when asked how the last few months have been sign he re-joined Charlton in the summer. The Addicks academy graduate returned after six years at West Brom, where he had turned down a new deal. "It all aligned at the time and hopefully it's still aligned at the end of the season," he added of why he decided to come back to south London. When Grant left The Valley in January 2019 for Huddersfield, it was not well-received by some Charlton fans. But seven years and three clubs later, the 29-year-old is an experienced and established Championship player. messages.text: McDermott blasts 'harsh' RL World Cup format

metadata.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has branded the format of the Rugby League World Cup as "harsh" with his side up against it to progress.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England head coach Brian McDermot blasts 'harsh' format and explains Mikey Lewis absence | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England head coach Brian McDermot blasts 'harsh' format and explains Mikey Lewis absence England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am) in their second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; Coach Brian McDermott discussed World Cup format and Mikey Lewis' continued absence ahead of weekend clash Thursday 22 October 2026 15:22, UK Image: England coach Brian McDermott has branded the Rugby League World Cup format 'harsh,' with his side up against it to progress England head coach Brian McDermott has branded the format of the Rugby League World Cup as "harsh" with his side up against it to progress. Last Saturday's loss to Tonga means England must hope Tonga beat Samoa in their final group game next week in order to stand any realistic chance of reaching the semi-finals. That scenario would leave England and Samoa to be separated by points difference - a particularly tough ask for McDermott's men given the Samoans started their campaign with a crushing 78-4 win over France. "The jeopardy is losing one game is so harsh, it's almost like we don't get another chance to straighten things out," said McDermott, whose side face the French in their second group game in Perth on Saturday.
